descripcion_es: Turning verbs and adjectives into nouns for a formal, compact style: the introduction of…, the rise in…
resumen: Nominalisation turns actions and qualities into nouns (introduce → the introduction of). It makes the text more impersonal, dense and formal, typical of reports, the press and academic presentations.

explicacion.texto: Compare: Prices rose sharply, so consumers spent less → The sharp rise in prices led to a fall in consumer spending. The verb becomes a noun, the adverb becomes an adjective and the subject becomes a complement with of or an adjective.

filas: in (a rise in prices) / of (a rise of 5%)
a fall / a decrease / a decline

items: The agent is expressed with of, by or a possessive: the government's decision, the decision by the government.
Adverbs become adjectives: rose dramatically → a dramatic rise.
Useful verbs for linking nominalisations: lead to, result in, cause, give rise to, stem from, be due to.
Don't overdo it: a sentence with too many nouns becomes opaque. In speech, it is best to alternate.

ejemplos.frase: The introduction of the new timetable caused widespread confusion.
ejemplos.traduccion: La implantación del nuevo horario causó una confusión generalizada.

ejemplos.frase: There has been a significant increase in tourism over the past decade.
ejemplos.traduccion: Se ha producido un aumento considerable del turismo en la última década.

ejemplos.frase: His refusal to cooperate delayed the investigation.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su negativa a colaborar retrasó la investigación.

ejemplos.frase: The closure of the factory resulted in the loss of 300 jobs.
ejemplos.traduccion: El cierre de la fábrica supuso la pérdida de 300 empleos.

ejemplos.frase: The lack of rain has led to a shortage of water.
ejemplos.traduccion: La falta de lluvia ha provocado escasez de agua.

ejemplos.frase: Her appointment as director was welcomed by the staff.
ejemplos.traduccion: Su nombramiento como directora fue bien recibido por la plantilla.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: To say what increases, use in; of is kept for the amount (an increase of 5%).

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: The government's decision of raising taxes
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: The government's decision to raise taxes
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Decision goes with to + infinitive, not with of + -ing.
The noun from grow is growth.

ejercicios.frase: There was a sharp fall ___ unemployment last year.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table shows that fall, decrease and decline go with in to indicate what goes down. The clue is unemployment: it is what goes down, not a figure. So you say “a sharp fall in unemployment”. The typical mistake is to translate Spanish “descenso del paro” literally with of, which in English is kept for the amount (a fall of 2%).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A fall in + what goes down.
ejercicios.traduccion: El año pasado hubo un fuerte descenso del paro.

por_opcion.of: Incorrect. With fall, of introduces the amount (“a fall of 3%”), not what goes down; it is a literal translation of Spanish “del paro”.
por_opcion.in: Correct. A fall in + what goes down: a fall in unemployment.
por_opcion.on: Incorrect. On is not used with fall to indicate what goes down.
por_opcion.at: Incorrect. At does not form a collocation with fall in this sense.

glosario.definicion_l: the state of being unemployed or not having a job
(of something seen or heard) clearly defined · ending in a sharp point

ejercicios.frase: Sales showed an increase ___ 12% compared with 2023.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table distinguishes in (a rise in prices) from of (a rise of 5%), and the typical mistakes sum it up: of is kept for the amount. The clue is the figure 12%: it expresses the size of the increase, not what increases (which is already the subject, sales). So “an increase of 12%”. By is used with the verb (increase by 12%), not with the noun.
ejercicios.traduccion: Las ventas registraron un aumento del 12 % con respecto a 2023.

por_opcion.in: Incorrect. In introduces what increases (an increase in sales), not the figure.
por_opcion.of: Correct. An increase of + figure gives the size of the increase.
por_opcion.by: Incorrect. By is used with the verb (“sales increased by 12%”); with the noun the figure goes with of.
por_opcion.on: Incorrect. On does not express the amount of an increase.

glosario.significado: en comparación con, con respecto a

ejercicios.frase: The company's ___ to adapt led to its collapse.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes fail → the failure, with of or to + infinitive. The clue is the genitive “The company's”, which requires a noun after it, and the “to adapt” that follows: failure to + infinitive means “not managing to, not being able to”. In this way the whole phrase works as the subject of led to. Fail is a verb, and failing or failed are verb or adjective forms.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: You need the noun: failure to + infinitive.
ejercicios.traduccion: La incapacidad de la empresa para adaptarse provocó su quiebra.

por_opcion.fail: Incorrect. Fail is the verb; after the genitive you need a noun.
por_opcion.failing: Incorrect. Failing exists as a noun (“a weakness, a fault”), but it is not used with to + infinitive in this sense.
por_opcion.failure: Correct. Failure is the noun from fail and goes with to + infinitive: failure to adapt.
por_opcion.failed: Incorrect. Failed is the past simple or past participle (a failed attempt) and cannot be the head after the genitive.

glosario.definicion_l: an abrupt failure of function or complete physical exhaustion · a natural event caused by something suddenly falling down or caving in

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the noun formed from the verb in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The ___ (approve) of the budget was delayed until March.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes approve → the approval, with of. The clue is the article The and the preposition of: you need a noun that names the action of approving. The suffix is -al: approval. The object of the action (the budget) now goes with of, as the sheet explains.
ejercicios.traduccion: La aprobación del presupuesto se retrasó hasta marzo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Approbation exists, but it is old-fashioned and means “moral approval”; the approval of a budget is approval.
Spelling mistake: approval is written with double p.
It does not exist in English; the noun from approve is approval.

glosario.definicion_l: a sum of money allocated for a particular purpose · a summary of intended expenditures along with proposals for how to meet them
time during which some action is awaited · the act of delaying; inactivity resulting in something being put off until a later time

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the noun formed from the adjective in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The ___ (available) of cheap credit fuelled the housing boom.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes available → the availability, with of. The clue is the article The and the of that follows, which require the noun. The suffix -able becomes -ability: availability. Nominalisation turns the idea “cheap credit was available” into a compact subject, typical of economic analysis.
ejercicios.traduccion: La disponibilidad de crédito barato alimentó el auge inmobiliario.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is not used; the noun from available is availability.
A literal translation of Spanish “disponibilidad”: in English it is availability.
Spelling mistake: it is written availability, with -vai-.

glosario.definicion_l: a substance that can be consumed to produce energy · provide with a combustible substance that provides energy

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the noun formed from the verb in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: The ___ (reduce) in working hours was welcomed by employees.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes reduce → the reduction, with in or of. The clue is the article The and the preposition in, which introduces what is reduced (working hours). The suffix is -tion: reduction. Notice that you say reduction in working hours, just like a fall in unemployment.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los empleados acogieron con agrado la reducción de la jornada laboral.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It does not exist; the noun from reduce is reduction.
After the and before in you need the full noun reduction; reducing would be a verb form.
Reduce is the verb; the instruction asks for the noun formed from it.

glosario.definicion_l: giving pleasure or satisfaction or received with pleasure or freely granted · the state of being welcome

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the noun formed from the adjective in brackets.
ejercicios.frase: Investors showed great ___ (reluctant) to take risks.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes reluctant → reluctance, with to + infinitive. The clue is great, an adjective that requires a noun after it, and the “to take risks” that follows. The suffix -ant becomes -ance: reluctance. It is uncountable and takes no article.
ejercicios.traduccion: Los inversores se mostraron muy reacios a asumir riesgos.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is not used; the noun is reluctance.
Reluctant is the adjective; after great you need the noun reluctance.
It does not exist; the correct suffix is -ance: reluctance.

glosario.definicion_l: (physics) opposition to magnetic flux (analogous to electric resistance) · a certain degree of unwillingness

ejercicios.frase: Europe's dependence ___ imported energy remains high.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes depend on → dependence on: the noun keeps the preposition of the verb. The clue is dependence, which always takes on. Translating Spanish “dependencia de” literally leads to of, which is wrong here. The possessor (Europe) goes in the genitive, as the sheet indicates.
ejercicios.traduccion: La dependencia de Europa de la energía importada sigue siendo elevada.

errores_previstos.explicacion: A literal translation of Spanish “dependencia de”; dependence keeps the preposition of the verb: on.
From is not used with dependence; the preposition is on.
In does not form a collocation with dependence; you say dependence on.

glosario.definicion_l: stay the same; remain in a certain state · continue in a place, position, or situation

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite as a single sentence starting with “The closure of the bridge”.
ejercicios.frase: They closed the bridge, which caused traffic chaos.
respuestas: The closure of the bridge caused traffic chaos.
The closure of the bridge led to traffic chaos.
The closure of the bridge resulted in traffic chaos.
ejercicios.explicacion: The general mechanism in the sheet applies: the verb becomes a noun and the object goes with of. Close → the closure of the bridge, and the rest of the information (which caused traffic chaos) becomes the predicate: caused traffic chaos. The impersonal subject they, which added no information, disappears and the sentence becomes more concise. Instead of caused, led to and resulted in also work, as they express the same cause-and-effect relationship.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Close → the closure of; the rest of the sentence becomes the predicate.
ejercicios.traduccion: El cierre del puente provocó un caos circulatorio.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The closure of the bridge, which caused traffic chaos.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It is not a complete sentence: the main verb is missing; which turns the rest into a subordinate clause.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The closure of the bridge it caused traffic chaos.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The word it is unnecessary: the subject is already the closure of the bridge and is not repeated with a pronoun.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The closing of the bridge caused traffic chaos.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Closing exists, but the instruction asks you to start with “The closure of the bridge”.

glosario.definicion_l: approaching a particular destination; a coming closer; a narrowing of a gap · a rule for limiting or ending debate in a deliberative body

ejercicios.enunciado: Rewrite as a single sentence starting with “The sharp rise”.
ejercicios.frase: Prices rose sharply, and this worried consumers.
respuestas: The sharp rise in prices worried consumers.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the example in the sheet: the verb rose becomes a noun (rise), the adverb sharply becomes an adjective (sharp) and the subject prices becomes a complement with in. The second clause, “this worried consumers”, becomes the predicate: worried consumers. The result is “The sharp rise in prices worried consumers”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Verb → noun, adverb → adjective, subject → complement with in.
ejercicios.traduccion: La fuerte subida de los precios preocupó a los consumidores.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The sharp rise of prices worried consumers.
errores_previstos.explicacion: With rise, what goes up goes with in; of is kept for the amount (a rise of 5%).

errores_previstos.respuesta: The sharply rise in prices worried consumers.
errores_previstos.explicacion: When you nominalise, the adverb becomes an adjective: sharp, not sharply.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The sharp rise in prices, and this worried consumers.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the coordination and leaves the sentence without a main verb; worried must be the verb of the sharp rise.

ejercicios.frase: The decision of closing the school angered parents.
respuestas: The decision to close the school angered parents.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table shows that decide → the decision goes with to + infinitive (or with on). The clue is “decision of closing”, a literal translation of Spanish “la decisión de cerrar”. In English decision does not take of + -ing; the correction is “The decision to close the school”.
ejercicios.traduccion: La decisión de cerrar el colegio indignó a los padres.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The decision of closing the school angered parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: decision goes with to + infinitive, not with of + -ing.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The decision of close the school angered parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: It keeps the literal of; decision takes to + infinitive.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The decision to closing the school angered parents.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After to you need the infinitive close, not the -ing form.

glosario.definicion_l: a strong emotion; a feeling that is oriented toward some real or supposed grievance · the state of being angry

ejercicios.frase: There has been a steady grow in online sales.
respuestas: There has been a steady growth in online sales.
There has been steady growth in online sales.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes grow → the growth, and the typical mistakes warn about “the economic grow”. The clue is the article a and the adjective steady, which require a noun: grow is only a verb. The correction is growth, with or without the article, because growth is usually uncountable but accepts a when it goes with an adjective that describes it.
ejercicios.traduccion: Ha habido un crecimiento constante de las ventas por internet.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There has been a steady grow in online sales.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This leaves the sentence uncorrected: grow is a verb; the noun is growth.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There has been a steady growing in online sales.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Growing is not used as a noun for the growth of sales; the word is growth.

errores_previstos.respuesta: There has been a steady growth of online sales.
errores_previstos.explicacion: To say what grows, in is preferred: growth in online sales.

glosario.definicion_l: not subject to change or variation especially in behavior · not liable to fluctuate or especially to fall

ejercicios.frase: The ___ of the new law took many companies by surprise.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table includes introduce → the introduction, with of. The clue is the position between The and of: only a noun can fill that slot. In this context introduction means the implementation or entry into force of a rule, not the introduction of a book. Take by surprise means to catch someone unprepared.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After the and before of you need a noun.
ejercicios.traduccion: La entrada en vigor de la nueva ley sorprendió a muchas empresas.

por_opcion.introduce: Incorrect. Introduce is the verb; between the and of you need a noun.
por_opcion.introducing: Incorrect. Introducing is an -ing verb form; with the and of the full noun is introduction.
por_opcion.introduction: Correct. Introduction is the noun from introduce and goes with of: the introduction of the new law.
por_opcion.introductory: Incorrect. Introductory is an adjective and cannot be the head of the phrase.

respuestas: The lack of investment led to a decline in quality
ejercicios.explicacion: The sheet recommends linking nominalisations with verbs such as lead to, result in or cause. Here there are two: “The lack of investment” as the subject and “a decline in quality” as the complement, joined by led to. Decline goes with in for what goes down, like fall. The order is subject, linking verb and consequence.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Two nominalisations linked by led to.
ejercicios.traduccion: La falta de inversión provocó un deterioro de la calidad.

errores_previstos.respuesta: A decline in quality led to the lack of investment
errores_previstos.explicacion: It reverses cause and effect: the lack of investment is the cause of the decline.

errores_previstos.respuesta: The lack in investment led to a decline of quality
errores_previstos.explicacion: It swaps the prepositions: lack goes with of and decline with in.

descripcion_larga_es: Nominalisation turns verbs and adjectives into nouns (introduce becomes the introduction of, available becomes the availability of) to build denser, more impersonal and more formal sentences. It is the central feature of the English of reports, the economic press and academic presentations, exactly the register a candidate needs. Spanish speakers find it hard to choose the correct preposition (a rise in prices, not of), the right suffix (growth, failure, reluctance) and the construction with to + infinitive.

contexto.que_es: It is the process by which an action or a quality is expressed with a noun instead of a verb or an adjective. When you nominalise, the verb becomes a noun (rise, failure, reduction), the adverb becomes an adjective (sharply → sharp) and the subject becomes a complement with of, by, in or a possessive.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is the hallmark of formal written English and of technical presentations: it lets you condense several ideas into one sentence and chain causes and effects with verbs such as lead to or result in. In a C1 exam it is highly valued, but clumsy use (wrong preposition, badly formed noun) is noticed straight away. Overusing it, however, makes the text opaque.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It appears when describing data and trends (a sharp fall in unemployment), when summarising decisions (the approval of the budget) and when relating causes and consequences in reports. Spanish speakers translate “el aumento de los precios” literally as “increase of the prices” and “la decisión de cerrar” as “decision of closing”; English needs increase in prices and decision to close.
